t.E150d.agn: IARC classifies 4-MEI in Group 2B (possibly carcinogenic to humans) on the basis of animal studies. The Hong Kong Centre for Food Safety states that normal cola consumption is not expected to cause health problems because of 4-MEI.
t.E150d.body: In rats given a single oral dose, most of the high-molecular-weight colour components of caramel IV were not absorbed; within 96 hours almost all of the dose was excreted in the faeces and only 1–2% in the urine.
t.E150d.eff.0.a: No problem expected with normal consumption
t.E150d.eff.0.t: 4-MEI, which may form during production, is in IARC Group 2B on the basis of animal studies; the Hong Kong Centre for Food Safety does not expect health problems with normal cola consumption
t.E150d.eval: The production by-product 4-methylimidazole (4-MEI) is classified by IARC in Group 2B (possibly carcinogenic); it is common in cola and similar carbonated drinks.
t.E150d.prod: Obtained by heat treatment of carbohydrates together with sulphite and ammonium compounds. Because ammonia compounds are used (class IV), a by-product called 4-methylimidazole (4-MEI) may form during production.
t.E150d.summary: A caramel colour obtained by heating sugar with sulphite and ammonia compounds. It is the most widely used caramel in cola and other dark-coloured drinks.
t.E150d.what: Gives food a colour ranging from light brown to dark brown.
